source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 4 / line 6 Pension and Annuity Subtraction (PDF p.18-19 Line 4 bullets; p.19-20 Line 6; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 4 and 6), 65 or older: '$24,000 minus any amount entered on line 3'; DR 0104AD line 3 / line 5 Social Security Benefits (PDF p.18 Line 3; p.19 Line 5; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 3 and 5); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (you) 30,000.00 + interest 10,000.00 + taxable Social Security 17,000.00 = 57,000.00. Taxable Social Security on gross benefits 20,000.00 (you): federal SS worksheet (given): half of benefits 10,000.00 + other income 40,000.00 = 50,000.00; less 25,000.00 = 25,000.00; line 11 = 16,000.00; line 13 = half of smaller of 25,000.00 and 9,000.00 = 4,500.00; line 14 = 4,500.00; line 15 = 85% x 16,000.00 = 13,600.00; line 16 = 18,100.00; 85% of benefits = 17,000.00; taxable Social Security = 17,000.00. Federal taxable income = 57,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 39,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 39,250.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 57,000.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 39,250.00. DR 0104AD: Line 3 (primary taxpayer, age 72, 65 or older): entire taxable Social Security 17,000.00. Line 4 (primary taxpayer, age 72, 65 or older): taxable pension, annuity and IRA income 30,000.00; limit 24,000.00 minus line 3 17,000.00 = 7,000.00; subtraction = smaller of 30,000.00 and 7,000.00 = 7,000.00. Line 22 subtotal = 24,000.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 24,000.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 39,250.00 - 24,000.00 = 15,250.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 15,250.00 = 671.00 (the tax table row over 15,200.00 but not over 15,300.00, PDF p.34, gives 671.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 671.00.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.

The pension cap is reduced by each person's taxable Social Security (the record's line 3 or line 5 subtraction). That equals the printed rule whenever the Social Security subtraction is the person's full taxable benefit, and also when it is limited to 20,000 (the 55-64 pension cap is then used up either way). How a joint return's taxable Social Security (Form 1040 line 6b) is split between spouses is left to a Department publication not in the sources; the projection splits it the way the household's facts do.
